ticket.title: Wire miter deps --layers --check into the Tier 3 outfeed gate
ticket.description:
MTR-19 built the lateral-edge gate and it works (exit 0 clean, exit 1 naming the edge when an allowlist entry is removed), but nothing calls it yet, so a new cross-product edge can still land silently.

GB-200 phase 1b left this as an open decision with a recommendation: wire it into `outfeed gate` (Tier 3) rather than per-repo CI, because the layer map spans 42 crates across 11 repositories and no single repository can evaluate it. Only outfeed sees the whole suite, and per-repo CI would need the sibling checkouts.

The wiring is deliberately not done in MTR-19: it lives in outfeed-cli, outside that ticket scope. Measured baseline to assert against: 84 downward, 23 lateral (all allowlisted under GB-204), 0 upward.

verification_receipt.summary: outfeed gate now runs the suite layer check as a Tier 3 step between contracts and lockfiles. Because the gate runs per repository and the layer map spans 42 crates across 11 repositories, the step skips with a stated reason wherever .gaugeblock/miter/layers-allowlist.toml is absent, and otherwise delegates to the shared Process path so a non-zero miter deps --layers --check exit fails the gate. 7 gate tests pass, including one pinning the skip and its message; the step count assertion was made structural so adding a step no longer breaks it. Pre-existing release_all failures in this environment are InsufficientDiskSpace (116 MB free), not code.
